Catherine Muyonga
Science communications specialist, scuba diver, underwater cinematographer
Meet the client
How do we ensure that the people closest to the ocean are also the strongest voices shaping its future?

Catherine found the ocean by chance, then realised that telling credible, authentic ocean stories meant understanding the ocean itself — a journey that took her underwater quite literally. Coastal communities taught her to swim in open water, take underwater photographs, and eventually take up diving.

Since then, she has co-created films with coastal communities, built communications strategies for ocean NGOs, and mentored local fisher communities in telling their own conservation stories — always putting people at the centre and letting them lead.

Site and context

Mombasa coast, Kenya

Where coastal landscape, marine life and tropical climate shape the retreat experience.

Site location

Set along the Mombasa coast, defined by the Indian Ocean, sandy beaches, coral reefs and tropical vegetation — a strong link between the built environment and the marine landscape, ideal for a retreat centred on diving, exploration and relaxation.

Climate

A warm, humid tropical coastal climate for much of the year. The design responds with natural ventilation, generous shade, comfortable outdoor spaces and controlled solar exposure.

Design response

Open, breathable, and connected to nature — ocean views, shaded transitional spaces and an understated coastal material palette create a retreat that feels integrated with its surroundings.

Ocean — connection Climate — comfort Landscape — immersion Marine life — inspiration Retreat — restoration

The retreat experience

Three rooms, one journey

Each space carries its own purpose, function and atmosphere, while contributing to a single guest experience.

The Coastal LoungeThe living room
The living room

The Coastal Lounge

Inspired by the serene beauty of the Swahili coast and the rhythm of the Indian Ocean. Natural texture, warm timber and soft earthy tones build a relaxed, luxurious atmosphere, while curated ocean photography celebrates the client's passion for diving and exploration.

  • L-shaped sofa and woven carpet anchoring an open seating group
  • Wall reserved for ocean and diver-themed artwork
  • Rattan pendant lighting and a wicker storage trunk
  • Palm-embroidered cushions and driftwood accents
Living room + office floor plan
Floor planScale 1:50
The office space

The Explorer's Study

A refined workspace inspired by the adventurous spirit of a female marine diver. Enclosed within the living room, it holds a sense of privacy while staying connected to the open-plan space — underwater photography, books and travel pieces reflecting a life spent exploring the sea.

  • Work desk placed at the window, for natural light
  • Built-in bookshelf and an underwater photography gallery wall
  • Reading corner with an accent chair
  • Reeded timber storage with brass hardware
Explorer's Study floor plan
Floor planScale 1:50
The Explorer's StudyThe office space
The Coral NestThe bedroom
The bedroom

The Coral Nest

A cozy, serene bedroom inspired by the tranquility of the ocean. Soft neutral tones, natural timber and woven texture create a calming atmosphere, while layered bedding and organic material turn the room into a peaceful sanctuary.

  • Canopy bed with sheer drape and a natural-fibre jute rug
  • Built-in wardrobe and a full-length corner mirror
  • Accent chair with side table, and a low console dresser
  • Ocean-themed wall artwork above the bed
